title: Deploy-time quantization sensitivity sweep and adaptive rollback throttle
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a deploy-time evaluation sweep that measures end-to-end quality impact for AWQ/GPTQ int8 and int4 profiles, and implement an adaptive rollback throttle (auto-throttle) that gates rollout when cohort-level regressions exceed configurable thresholds.

Background: We regularly onboard quantized model variants to reduce unit cost. Past incidents showed subtle quality regressions after large config changes (batching/kv-cache + quant profile changes) and during rollouts, which were detected late by manual evals. We need an automated, reproducible, deploy-time check with per-route/cohort sensitivity and an operational auto-throttle that can pause or roll back a rollout when quality deltas cross thresholds.

Scope and deliverables:
- Evaluation harness extension: add a DeploySweep runner that runs targeted prompts across prioritized cohorts (0-latency-critical, high-precision, med) with AWQ and GPTQ profiles for int8/int4.
- Metricization: compute cohort-level delta metrics (EM-like, BLEU-ish for structured outputs, semantic-similarity using embedding cosine, KL on token distributions) and a combined fidelity score.
- Threshold tuning: implement a small calibration job that synthesizes perturbations to translate metric deltas into actionable thresholds (per-cohort, per-route).
- Adaptive rollback throttle: service that subscribes to deploy sweep results and enforces policy (pause rollout, reduce concurrency, fallback to higher-precision variant) when thresholds breached.
- CI/CD integration: run the sweep in pre-release canary stage and fail canary if strong regressions found.
- Observability & runbook: dashboard with delta heatmaps, cohort trends, and runbook for manual override and incident postmortems.

Acceptance criteria:
- The DeploySweep runs in under 12 minutes for a canary (sampled prompts) and produces a fidelity report JSON compatible with existing eval pipelines.
- Threshold calibration tool outputs per-cohort thresholds with recommended actions.
- Adaptive rollback throttle successfully pauses a canary rollout in the staging environment when thresholds are exceeded in 3 consecutive checks.
- Dashboard and alerting (pager + Slack channel) are configured and tested with synthetic regression events.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Running comprehensive sweeps increases CI time and cost; we mitigate by sampling prompts per cohort and running full sweeps only on major model/config changes.
- Metric selection is approximate; we'll iterate on metric weights based on human review panels.
- False positives could block rollouts; we will allow manual overrides and conservative tuning during initial rollout.

Implementation notes and artifacts:
- Eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/418 (WIP)
- Runtime gating PR for throttle integration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1245 (draft)
- Design doc / runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deploy+Quant+Sensitivity+Sweep+Runbook
comments: 2025-11-03 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial scope sketched after postmortem from incident on 2025-10-18 where an int8 AWQ rollout caused a 2.3% drop in semantic-similarity for the checkout cohort. Recommended building deploy-time checks and an auto-throttle. Linked incident notes in Confluence.

2025-11-06 - Marco Nguyen: Spiked on candidate metric set. Ran a 1k prompt sample comparing fp16 vs int8-awq vs int4-gptq across three cohorts. Observed that embedding cosine captures semantic degradation more reliably than token-level BLEU for our chat routes. Saved artifacts to s3://rwd-quant-evals/2025-11-06/.

2025-11-10 - Priya Rao (PM review): Reviewed metrics. Requested explicit thresholds for high-precision cohort (<=0.7% allowable cosine drop) and stricter failure actions for customer-facing routes. Asked for dashboard prototypes before integrating auto-throttle.

2025-11-12 - Design feedback (Liam Chen): Suggested adding a compact human-review panel for cases where metric deltas are near threshold to reduce false positives; proposed a 'manual hold' channel in the console rollout UI.

2025-11-15 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented DeploySweep runner skeleton and wired sample dataset selection logic. Benchmarked sweep runtime: 9 minutes for 300 prompts across 3 cohorts using a dedicated canary pool. Push: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/commit/9fd2b4c.

2025-11-18 - Results: initial calibration job produced a per-cohort recommended threshold table. Observed that int4-GPTQ has bimodal failures on the high-precision cohort; flagged for possible per-layer gating instead of global rollback. Stored calibration run: s3://rwd-quant-evals/calibration/nov18.json.
2025-11-20 - Security note (Maya Singh): Confirmed no user PII in sampled prompt sets; data handling reviewed. No security review required for this initial phase.

2025-11-22 - Integration test: Deployed adaptive throttle service to staging and ran synthetic regression event. Throttle paused the rollout after 2 consecutive failed checks and posted alert to #infra-quant. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1245.

2025-11-25 - PM check-in (Priya Rao): Requested adding a cooldown policy and a 'grace-check' that triggers a human-review task instead of immediate rollback for borderline cases. Also asked to include cost vs. quality tradeoff notes in the runbook.

2025-11-28 - Next steps (Marco Nguyen): Finish CI integration to run DeploySweep as a pre-canary gate (ETA 2025-12-03). Iterate metric weights with human panel scheduled 2025-12-05. Plan to run a controlled canary on a subset of traffic in week of 2025-12-08 and evaluate with the dashboard.
